messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Passing pointers to Nimble functions
parts:
Hi

I am trying to explore what is and is not possible with Compiled_Model and Compiled_Mcmc_Output$mvSample  objects.

For example, once an MCMC has run, it can be desirable to take a line of the MCMC output, plug it back into the model and do something with it - perhaps simulate some dependent nodes or calculate log-likelihoods.

This is easy in R, but I can't see how to do it in a nimble function which is also to be compiled.  But, given the potential speed gain it would surely be desirable to be able to do so. I specifically mean after the MCMC has ran.

I've written a toy script based on the pump example. After running the MCMC the script revisits each MCMC sample and uses the compiled model to re-create the log-likelihood via cPump$calculate().  You can easily imagine other examples where "simulate" is used too, but I left out simulate just to keep things simple.

So the question is, is it possible to write a nimble function, & compile it, that does the same job as the loop in the script?  I can't see how to start because presumably I should be passing two pointers to the nimble function and I don't know if that is possible.

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Passing pointers to Nimble functions
parts:
Hi David,

Yes, what you want to do is possible.  You can use the copy (or, equivalently, nimCopy) function to copy arbitrary nodes from a row of a modelValues object into the model.  Then you can use calculate or other model operations.  You will need to make the uncompiled model and modelValues be arguments to the setup code.  The compiled versions will be used by the corresponding compiled nimbleFunction(s).  (Alternatively you could use the MCMC as an argument to the setup code and the access the mvSamples modelValues object in that.)

Short of writing up a fresh example for you, I will first point you to the importance sampling example in our paper accepted to JCGS that is available here on arxiv:
http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10618600.2016.1172487.  If that doesn’t illustrate what you need please let us know and we can clarify further.

Perry
